original_question: Fix an integer d, let G = SL_d/μ_d, let V = Sym^d(k^d) be the d-th symmetric power of the natural d-dimensional representation of SL_d viewed as a G-module, and let σ be the automorphism of G induced by the automorphism g ↦ (g^T)^−1 of SL_d. Are the G-varieties V and σV birationally G-isomorphic?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 4 (“Birationally nonequivalent linear actions”), posed as a special case of Problem 3. ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s singled-out special case almost verbatim: it uses the same group G = SL_d/μ_d, the same module V = Sym^d(k^d), the same automorphism induced by g ↦ (g^T)^(-1), and asks exactly whether V and σV are birationally G-isomorphic. ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
missing_details: The paper’s standing assumption for this section is that all algebraic varieties are over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0; your draft names k but does not state these hypotheses. ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

To be fully stand-alone, σV should be defined as the twist of the G-action by σ: it is the same underlying variety as V, with action g · v := σ(g) acting through the original action on V. ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

“Birationally G-isomorphic” should be spelled out as “G-equivariantly birationally isomorphic.” ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

It is implicit that V is a G-module because the natural SL_d-action on Sym^d(k^d) factors through SL_d/μ_d; saying “with the natural G-action” makes this cleaner and closer to the paper. ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

If you want the surrounding motivation from Problems 2 and 3 to be visible, the paper notes that for d > 3 the stabilizers of points in general position in V are trivial; however, this is contextual and not part of the formal statement of Problem 4 itself. ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let d ≥ 1 be an integer, let G := SL_d/μ_d, and let V := Sym^d(k^d) with its natural G-action. Let σ be the automorphism of G induced by the automorphism g ↦ (g^T)^(-1) of SL_d, and let σV denote the corresponding twist of V, i.e. the same underlying variety with G-action g · v := σ(g) acting through the original action on V. Are the G-varieties V and σV G-equivariantly birationally isomorphic? ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
justification: The draft is aiming at Popov’s Problem 4, not at a broader neighboring problem. In Section 1, Popov first formulates Problem 3 about the existence of a connected semisimple group G, a finite-dimensional G-module V, and an automorphism σ such that V and σV are not birationally G-isomorphic, and then immediately isolates the concrete case G = SL_d/μ_d, V = Sym^d(k^d), with σ induced by g ↦ (g^T)^(-1), as Problem 4. The nearby context also supplies the standing field hypothesis and the definition of twisting by σ. The note after Problem 4 explains that for d > 3 the stabilizer in general position in V is trivial, which ties this example back to Problem 3, but Popov does not impose d > 3 in the formal wording of Problem 4. ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
